limitations: The variance-level three-cornered-hat method and unsigned-incidence rank theorem are classical and are not claimed as new. The novelty claim is restricted to the distribution-level sparse-graph identification theorem, sharp Gaussian bipartite alias, one-marginal latent reconstruction, and exact minimal comparison design under the stated symmetry and nonvanishing assumptions.
scientific_summary: For independent additive measurement errors with centrally symmetric nowhere-zero characteristic functions, marginal pairwise-difference laws identify all individual error distributions exactly when every connected component of the comparison graph contains an odd cycle. The criterion is sharp via Gaussian aliases on bipartite components, and m edges are necessary and sufficient for m>=3 instruments.
